elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Customer to terminate the entire Agreement for convenience at the end of any calendar month and does not limit that right to term-end.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (a) expressly requires prior written notice to IBM.

elements.element: The required Customer notice period is 30 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least one month, which is not a fixed 30-day period.

elements.element: Customer may make termination effective upon expiration of the 30-day notice period without an additional calendar-month-end restriction.
elements.evidence: Termination is permitted only at the end of a calendar month, which can delay effectiveness beyond the notice period.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination is not subject to an early-termination fee or penalty.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) expressly conditions termination on payment of applicable early termination charges, although those charges are capped.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: IBM must refund any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination, which provides the required time-based refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative clause grants a convenience-termination right only to Customer and contains no Vendor convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly grants Customer a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer termination requires no more than the acceptable 60–90-day fallback notice period.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least one month's written notice and may delay effectiveness until the next calendar-month end. This produces a shorter, and therefore Customer-favorable, notice burden that does not exceed the 90-day fallback maximum.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The aggregate early termination charges are expressly capped at three months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent from the rendered operative clause: no Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted, so Vendor cannot exercise such a right before term-end.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent from the rendered operative clause because Vendor receives no termination-for-convenience right at all.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback because Customer retains a convenience-termination right on notice no more burdensome than the fallback maximum, early termination charges are capped at three months' recurring Charges, and Vendor receives no convenience-termination right. It does not reach the preferred position because early termination charges remain payable, the notice period is not a fixed 30 days, and termination remains restricted to calendar-month end. The changes preserve unrelated terms, but they are not minimal to the completed fallback because the prepaid-fee refund is an additional preferred-level protection not needed for fallback compliance.
